units.zh: 時淮南太守文成侯蕭寧逃賊入吳，襄遣迎寧爲盟主，遣黯及兄子映公帥衆拒子仙。
units.en: At the time, Xiao Ning, Administrator of Huainan and Marquis Wencheng, fled the rebels and entered Wu. Xiang welcomed him as leader of the alliance, then sent Lu An and Xiang's nephew Yinggong to lead the troops against Song Zixian.
units.literal: At that time Xiao Ning, Administrator of Huainan and Marquis Wencheng, fled the rebels and entered Wu. Xiang sent to receive Ning as leader of the alliance, then dispatched Lu An and Xiang's elder brother's son Yinggong to lead the troops against Song Zixian.

units.zh: 子仙聞兵起，乃退還，與黯等戰於松江，黯敗走，吳下軍聞之，亦各奔散。
units.en: Zixian heard that troops had risen and then retreated; he fought with An and others at Song River; An was defeated and fled, and the armies below Wu, hearing of it, likewise each scattered and fled.
units.literal: Zixian heard that troops had risen and then retreated; he fought with An and others at Song River; An was defeated and fled, and the armies below Wu, hearing of it, likewise each scattered and fled.

units.zh: 襄匿于墓下，一夜憂憤卒，時年七十。
units.en: Xiang hid beneath a tomb; in one night grief and anger overcame him and he died at the age of seventy.
units.literal: Xiang hid beneath a tomb; in one night grief and anger overcame him and he died, aged seventy.

units.zh: 襄弱冠遭家禍，終身蔬食布衣，不聽音樂，口不言殺害五十許年。
units.en: Xiang in his weak-capping years suffered household calamity; all his life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, listened to no music, and for some fifty years did not speak of killing.
units.literal: Xiang in his weak-capping years suffered household calamity; all his life he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, listened to no music, and for some fifty years did not speak of killing.

units.zh: 侯景平，世祖追贈侍中、雲麾將軍。
units.en: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Shizu posthumously appointed him attendant-in-chief and cloud-banner general.
units.literal: When Hou Jing was pacified, Emperor Shizu posthumously appointed him Attendant-in-Chief and Cloud-Banner General.

units.zh: 以建義功，追封餘干縣侯，邑五百戶。
units.en: On account of his merit in raising righteous arms he was posthumously enfeoffed as marquis of Yugan county with a fief of five hundred households.
units.literal: On account of his merit in raising righteous arms he was posthumously enfeoffed as Marquis of Yugan county with a fief of five hundred households.

units.zh: 陳吏部尚書姚察曰：陸倕博涉文理，到洽匪躬貞勁，明山賓儒雅篤實，殷鈞靜素恬和，陸襄淳深孝性，雖任遇有異，皆列於名臣矣。
units.en: Yao Cha, director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Lu Chui broadly penetrated literary principles; Dao Qia with his whole person was upright and firm; Ming Shanbin was elegant in Confucian learning and sincere and solid; Yin Jun was quiet, plain, tranquil, and harmonious; Lu Xiang was pure, deep, and filial in nature—though their appointments differed, all were listed among famous ministers.
units.literal: Yao Cha, Director of the Ministry of Personnel of Chen, said: Lu Chui broadly penetrated literary principles; Dao Qia with his whole person was upright and firm; Ming Shanbin was elegant in Confucian learning and sincere and solid; Yin Jun was quiet, plain, tranquil, and harmonious; Lu Xiang was pure, deep, and filial in nature—though their appointments differed, all were listed among famous ministers.

units.en: [1] Endnote marker.
units.literal: [1] Endnote marker.

units.zh: 齊始安王遙光納焉。
units.en: Qi's Prince of Shi'an, Yaoguang, took her to wife.
units.literal: Prince of Shi'an Yaoguang of Qi took her in marriage.

units.zh: 遙光敗，入東昏宮。
units.en: When Yaoguang fell, she was taken into the Depraved Emperor's palace.
units.literal: When Yaoguang was defeated, she entered the Depraved Emperor's palace.

units.zh: 永明九年，雍州刺史王奐反，敕遣僧珍隸平北將軍曹虎西爲典籤，帶新城令。
units.en: In Yongming year nine, Yongzhou inspector Wang Huan rebelled; Sengzhen was sent west under Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu as Master of Documents, with concurrent magistracy of Xincheng.
units.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming, Inspector of Yongzhou Wang Huan rebelled; an edict sent Sengzhen under the Pacifying-the-North General Cao Hu west as Master of Documents, with concurrent charge of Xincheng.

units.zh: 尚書敬顯儁曰：「孔子云：『微管仲，吾其被發左衽矣』以此言之，右衽為是。」
units.en: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."
units.literal: Minister Jing Xianjun said, "Confucius said, 'Were it not for Guan Zhong, we would wear our hair loose and our lapel to the left.' By this reasoning the right lapel is correct."

units.zh: 乃遣國子博士范雲、舍人裴長穆等使石頭城詣高祖，高祖以稷爲侍中、左衛將軍。
units.en: Then he sent National University erudite Fan Yun, attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to see Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji attendant within and left palace guard general.
units.literal: Then he sent National University Erudite Fan Yun, Attendant Pei Changmu, and others to Stone City to present themselves to Gaozu; Gaozu made Ji Attendant Within and Left Palace Guard General.

units.zh: 戊戌，以護軍將軍陳顯達爲南兖州刺史，吳郡太守張岱爲中護軍。
units.en: On day wuxu, Chen Xianda, protector of the army, took South Yanzhou; Zhang Dai, administrator of Wu, became central protector of the army.
units.literal: On day wuxu, Protector of the Army Chen Xianda was made Inspector of South Yanzhou; Administrator of Wu Commandery Zhang Dai was made Central Protector of the Army.

units.zh: 范岫 傅昭 弟映 蕭琛 陸杲
units.en: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; his younger brother Ying; Xiao Chen; and Lu Gao
units.literal: Fan Xiu; Fu Zhao; younger brother Ying; Xiao Chen; Lu Gao

units.zh: 范岫字懋賓，濟陽考城人也。
units.en: Fan Xiu, styled Maobin, came from Kaocheng in Jiyang commandery.
units.literal: Fan Xiu, courtesy name Maobin, was a native of Kaocheng in Jiyang.

units.zh: 約常稱曰：「范公好事該博，胡廣無以加。」
units.en: Yue would often remark, “Master Fan delights in inquiry and knows everything—Hu Guang himself could add nothing.”
units.literal: Yue often said, “Master Fan is fond of learning and thoroughly informed; even Hu Guang could not surpass him.”

units.zh: 南鄉范雲謂人曰：「諸君進止威儀，當問范長頭。」
units.en: Fan Yun of Nanxiang told people, “For how to advance, withdraw, and comport yourselves, ask Long-Head Fan.”
units.literal: Fan Yun of Nanxiang told others, “Gentlemen, for questions of deportment and ritual bearing, you should ask Long-Head Fan.”

units.zh: 泰始中，起家奉朝請。
units.en: During the Taishi reign he began his career as a palace attendant.
units.literal: In the Taishi era he first entered office as a court attendant.

units.zh: 累遷臨海、長城二縣令，驃騎參軍，尚書刪定郎，護軍司馬，齊司徒竟陵王子良記室參軍。
units.en: He rose through a series of posts: magistrate of Linhai and Changcheng, staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry General, revising clerk in the Department of State Affairs, army aide to the Protector-General, and recorder on the staff of Qi’s Minister over the Masses, Prince Ziliang of Jingling.
units.literal: He was promoted in succession to magistrate of Linhai and Changcheng counties, staff officer to the Rapid Cavalry General, revising clerk in the Department of State Affairs, army aide to the Protector-General, and recorder on the staff of Prince Ziliang of Jingling, Minister over the Masses of Qi.

units.zh: 梁臺建，爲度支尚書。
units.en: When the Liang provisional government was set up, he became Minister of Revenue.
units.literal: When the Liang headquarters was established, he became Minister of Revenue.

units.zh: 岫文雖不逮約，而名行爲時輩所與，博涉多通，尤悉魏晉以來吉凶故事。
units.en: Xiu’s prose did not equal Yue’s, yet contemporaries respected his name and conduct; widely read and well informed, he was above all expert in ritual and omens from Wei and Jin times onward.
units.literal: Though Xiu’s writing did not match Yue’s, his reputation and conduct were acknowledged by contemporaries; he was broadly learned and especially versed in auspicious and inauspicious precedents from Wei and Jin onward.

units.zh: 遷國子博士。
units.en: He was appointed Erudite of the Imperial University.
units.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University.

units.zh: 所著文集、《禮論》、《雜儀》、《字訓》行於世。
units.en: His collected writings, Treatise on Rites, Miscellaneous Ritual Protocols, and Character Instruction circulated widely.
units.literal: His collected writings, Treatise on Rites, Miscellaneous Ritual Protocols, and Character Instruction circulated in the world.

units.zh: 八年，出爲晉陵太守，秩中二千石。
units.en: In year 8 he was sent out as administrator of Jinling, at the two-thousand-bushel rank.
units.literal: In the eighth year he went out as Administrator of Jinling, with rank of two thousand bushels.

units.zh: 出爲寧朔將軍、南蠻長史、南義陽太守，未赴職，遷右軍諮議參軍，郡如故。
units.en: He was sent out as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk of the Southern Man, and administrator of Southern Yiyang; before he assumed the post he was made staff adviser of the Right Army, retaining his nominal commandery rank.
units.literal: He went out as General Who Pacifies the North, chief clerk of the Southern Man, and Administrator of Southern Yiyang; before he took up the post he was transferred to staff adviser of the Right Army, while retaining his commandery title.

units.zh: 入爲給事黃門侍郎，遷御史中丞、領前軍將軍、南北兗二州大中正。
units.en: He entered court as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then became Censor-in-Chief, concurrently commanding the Vanguard General and serving as chief arbiter of pedigree for northern and southern Yan.
units.literal: He entered service as Attendant Gentleman at the Yellow Gate, then was transferred to Censor-in-Chief, concurrently commanding the Vanguard General and serving as chief arbiter of pedigree for both northern and southern Yan provinces.

units.zh: 七年，徙通直散騎常侍、右衛將軍，中正如故。
units.en: In year 7 he was transferred to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and General of the Right Guard, keeping his arbiter’s post.
units.literal: In the seventh year he was moved to Regular Attendant of Direct Communication and General of the Right Guard, retaining his post as chief arbiter.

units.zh: 天監五年，遷散騎常侍、光祿大夫，侍皇太子，給扶。
units.en: In Tianjian year 5 he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince with a ceremonial staff.
units.literal: In the fifth year of Tianjian he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, attending the crown prince with a staff granted.

units.zh: 二子褒，偉。
units.en: He left two sons, Bao and Wei.
units.literal: He had two sons, Bao and Wei.

units.zh: 岫早孤，事母以孝聞，與吳興沈約俱爲蔡興宗所禮。
units.en: Xiu was orphaned young but won renown for tending his mother with filial devotion; he and Shen Yue of Wuxing were alike held in esteem by Cai Xingzong.
units.literal: Xiu lost his father early; he was famed for filial service to his mother, and he and Shen Yue of Wuxing were both honored by Cai Xingzong.

units.zh: 文惠太子之在東宮，沈約之徒以文才見引，岫亦預焉。
units.en: When the Literary and Gracious Heir Apparent resided in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and others were recruited for their literary gifts, and Xiu was included among them.
units.literal: While the Literary and Gracious Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace, Shen Yue and his circle were drawn in for literary talent, and Xiu was among them.

units.zh: 永元末，出爲輔國將軍、冠軍晉安王長史，行南徐州事。
units.en: At the close of Yongyuan he was sent out as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Champion Prince of Jin’an, with charge of southern Xu.
units.literal: At the end of Yongyuan he went out as General Who Assists the State and chief clerk to the Champion Prince of Jin’an, acting for the southern Xu region.

units.zh: 六年，領太子左衛率。
units.en: In year 6 he also served as Left Commandant of the Crown Prince’s Guard.
units.literal: In the sixth year he concurrently held the post of Left Commandant of the Crown Prince’s Guard.

units.zh: 興宗爲安西將軍，引爲主簿。
units.en: When Xingzong was appointed General Who Pacifies the West, he brought Xiu in as his chief clerk.
units.literal: When Xingzong became General Who Pacifies the West, he took Xiu on as chief clerk.

units.zh: 爲長城令時，有梓材巾箱，至數十年，經貴遂不改易。
units.en: As magistrate of Changcheng he kept a catalpa-wood cap-box; for decades, even after he rose to high office, he never replaced it.
units.literal: When he was magistrate of Changcheng he had a catalpa-wood cap-box; for several decades, though he rose in rank, he never replaced it.

units.zh: 累遷太子家令。
units.en: He was promoted again to Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household.
units.literal: He was further promoted to Director of the Heir Apparent’s Household.

units.zh: 永明中，魏使至，有詔妙選朝士有詞辯者，接使於界首，以岫兼淮陰長史迎焉。
units.en: During Yongming an envoy from Wei arrived; the court was ordered to choose the most articulate officials to meet him at the frontier, and Xiu was sent as acting chief clerk of Huaiyin to receive him.
units.literal: In the Yongming era a Wei envoy arrived; an edict called for the finest court gentlemen skilled in debate to receive the envoy at the border, and Xiu was appointed acting chief clerk of Huaiyin to welcome him.

units.zh: 還遷尚書左丞，母憂去官，尋起攝職。
units.en: After returning he was made Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he resigned on his mother’s death but soon took up his duties again in an acting post.
units.literal: On his return he was promoted to Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs; he left office for his mother’s mourning, then soon resumed duties in an acting capacity.

units.zh: 除撫軍司馬。
units.en: He was appointed army aide to the Pacification General.
units.literal: He was appointed army aide to the Pacification General.

units.zh: 出爲建威將軍、安成內史。
units.en: He was sent out as General Who Establishes Might and interior secretary of Ancheng.
units.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might and Interior Secretary of Ancheng.

units.zh: 義師平京邑，承制徵爲尚書吏部郎，參大選。
units.en: After the righteous army took the capital, he was summoned under provisional authority to be Director of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in the great appointments.
units.literal: When the righteous army pacified the capital, he was summoned by provisional order to be Director of the Ministry of Personnel and took part in the great selection.

units.zh: 其年表致事，詔不許。
units.en: That same year he petitioned to retire; the throne refused.
units.literal: That year he memorialized to retire; the edict did not permit it.

units.zh: 九年，入爲祠部尚書，領右驍騎將軍，其年遷金紫光祿大夫，加親信二十人。
units.en: In year 9 he returned as Minister of Rites and concurrently commanded the Right Valiant Cavalry General; that year he was promoted to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon with twenty personal attendants.
units.literal: In the ninth year he entered as Minister of Rites, concurrently commanding the Right Valiant Cavalry General; that year he was transferred to Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with twenty personal attendants added.

units.zh: 十三年，卒官，時年七十五。
units.en: In year 13 he died in office, aged seventy-five.
units.literal: In the thirteenth year he died in office at the age of seventy-five.

units.zh: 賻錢五萬，布百匹。
units.en: The court granted fifty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral.
units.literal: Funeral gifts were fifty thousand cash and a hundred bolts of cloth.

units.zh: 在晉陵，惟作牙管筆一雙，猶以爲費。
units.en: At Jinling he allowed himself only one pair of ivory-barrel writing brushes—and even that he thought excessive.
units.literal: At Jinling he had made only one pair of ivory-barrel brushes, and even that he regarded as extravagant.

units.zh: 以岫多識前代舊事也。
units.en: — for Xiu knew the old precedents of earlier dynasties better than anyone.
units.literal: This was because Xiu knew so many stories of former ages.

units.zh: 岫身長七尺八寸，恭敬儼恪，進止以禮。
units.en: Xiu stood seven feet eight inches in height, grave and courteous in manner, every step governed by ritual.
units.literal: Xiu stood seven feet eight inches tall, reverent and dignified in bearing, advancing and withdrawing according to ritual.

units.zh: 自親喪之後，蔬食布衣以終身。
units.en: After mourning his parents he ate only plain food and wore coarse cloth for the rest of his days.
units.literal: After his parents’ mourning he ate vegetables and wore plain cloth for the rest of his life.

units.zh: 每所居官，恒以廉潔著稱。
units.en: In every post he held he was known for incorruptible conduct.
units.literal: In every office he held he was constantly famed for integrity and purity.

units.zh: 高祖宣，晉徵士。
units.en: His great-great-grandfather Xuan had been a Jin dynasty recluse-scholar.
units.literal: His great-great-grandfather Xuan was a reclusive scholar of Jin.

units.zh: 侯景遣將宋子仙據郢州，琳攻剋之，擒子仙。
units.en: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.
units.literal: Hou Jing sent General Song Zixian to hold Yingzhou; Lin attacked and took it, capturing Zixian.

units.zh: 與懷朔省事雲中司馬子如及秀容人劉貴、中山人賈顯智為奔走之友，懷朔戶曹史孫騰、外兵史侯景亦相友結。
units.en: He made running companions of Sima Ziru, affairs clerk at Huaishuo's Yunzhong desk, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan; Sun Teng, the garrison household clerk, and Hou Jing, clerk for external military affairs, joined their circle as well.
units.literal: With Sima Ziru, affairs clerk of Yunzhong at Huaishuo, Liu Gui of Xiurong, and Jia Xianzhi of Zhongshan he formed a band of comrades ready to run errands; Sun Teng, household clerk at Huaishuo, and Hou Jing, clerk in external military affairs, also joined in friendship.

units.zh: 董仲舒說上曰：「春秋它穀不書，至於麥禾不成則書之，以此見聖人於五穀最重麥與禾也。
units.en: Dong Zhongshu said to the emperor, 'In the Spring and Autumn Annals other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail to ripen it is recorded—showing that the sage gave greatest weight among the five grains to wheat and millet.
units.literal: Dong Zhongshu advised the emperor: 'In Spring and Autumn, other grains are not recorded, but when wheat and millet fail it is recorded-showing sages gave greatest weight among grains to wheat and millet.

units.zh: 仲舒死後，功費愈甚，天下虛耗，人復相食。
units.en: After his death, fiscal overextension intensified and extreme famine reappeared.
units.literal: After Zhongshu's death, expenditures and projects grew still greater; the realm emptied and consumed, people again ate one another.

units.zh: 武帝末年，悔征伐之事，乃封丞相為富民侯。
units.en: Late in Emperor Wu's reign, he regretted the campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.
units.literal: At Emperor Wu's late years, he regretted campaigns and then enfeoffed the Chancellor as Marquis of Enriching the People.

units.zh: 今關中俗不好種麥，是歲失春秋之所重，而損生民之具也。
units.en: Now the Guanzhong region dislikes planting wheat, and each year it neglects what the Annals values most, diminishing the people's means of livelihood.
units.literal: Now Guanzhong customs do not like sowing wheat, so each year they lose what Spring and Autumn values and damage the means of people's life.

units.zh: 願陛下幸詔大司農，使關中民益種宿麥，令毋後時。」
units.en: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture to have the people of Guanzhong plant more winter wheat and not miss the season.'
units.literal: May Your Majesty command the Grand Minister of Agriculture that Guanzhong people increase winter wheat and not miss seasonal timing.'

units.zh: 又言：「古者稅民不過什一，其求易共；
units.en: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;
units.literal: He also said: 'In antiquity taxing people was no more than one-tenth, easy to provide;

units.zh: 使民不過三日，其力易足。
units.en: and labor demands were limited enough to preserve household capacity.
units.literal: using people's labor no more than three days, their strength easy to suffice.

units.zh: 民財內足以養老盡孝，外足以事上共稅，下足以畜妻子極愛，故民說從上。
units.en: When household subsistence and obligations were simultaneously manageable, political obedience was voluntary.
units.literal: People's means were enough internally to care for elders and fulfill filiality, externally to serve superiors and taxes, below to support wives and children with full love, thus people gladly followed superiors.

units.zh: 至秦則不然，用商鞅之法，改帝王之制，除井田，民得賣買，富者田連仟伯，貧者亡立錐之地。
units.en: Qin reforms enabled severe land concentration and peasant landlessness.
units.literal: By Qin, not so: using Shang Yang's law, changing imperial kings' institutions, removing well-fields and allowing sale-purchase, rich fields stretched by tens and hundreds while poor had no ground to stand an awl.

units.zh: 又顓川澤之利，管山林之饒，荒淫越制，踰侈以相高；
units.en: State and elite control over resource rents fueled escalating luxury and inequality.
units.literal: It monopolized river-marsh profits and managed mountain-forest riches; wild excess surpassed norms, competing in extravagance.

units.zh: 邑有人君之尊，里有公侯之富，小民安得不困？
units.en: Sub-state elite power became so great that ordinary households had little room to survive.
units.literal: In towns there was lordly dignity, in villages marquis-level wealth-how could small people not be trapped?

units.zh: 又加月為更卒，已復為正，一歲屯戍，一歲力役，三十倍於古；
units.en: Labor conscription expanded to levels far above classical precedent.
units.literal: Further, adding monthly service as garrison labor and regular labor in sequence-one year frontier garrison, one year corvée-threefold ten times antiquity.

units.zh: 田租口賦，鹽鐵之利，二十倍於古。
units.en: The combined tax burden became vastly heavier than classical norms.
units.literal: Field rent and head tax, plus salt and iron revenues, were twenty times antiquity.

units.zh: 或耕豪民之田，見稅什五。
units.en: Tenancy under great households imposed predatory effective rates.
units.literal: Some tilled powerful households' fields and were taxed at five parts in ten.

units.zh: 故貧民常衣牛馬之衣，而食犬彘之食。
units.en: Peasant living standards degraded to near-animal subsistence.
units.literal: Thus poor people often wore ox-and-horse clothing and ate dog-and-pig food.

units.zh: 重以貪暴之吏，刑戮妄加，民愁亡聊，亡逃山林，轉為盜賊，赭衣半道，斷獄歲以千萬數。
units.en: Administrative violence plus poverty drove flight, crime, and mass penalization.
units.literal: Added to this were greedy violent officials with arbitrary executions, people grieving without livelihood, fleeing into hills and forests turning to banditry, red convict clothes half the roads, and yearly prison judgments in tens of millions.

units.zh: 漢興，循而未改。
units.en: Early Han inherited much of this structure before reform.
units.literal: When Han arose, it followed this and had not changed.

units.zh: 古井田法雖難卒行，宜少近古，限民名田，以澹不足，塞并兼之路。
units.en: Full restoration may be impossible, but partial anti-concentration land limits were urged.
units.literal: Though the old well-field law is hard to suddenly enact, one should somewhat approach antiquity: limit titled land holdings to relieve insufficiency and block annexation paths.

units.zh: 鹽鐵皆歸於民。
units.en: He advocated devolving salt and iron profits away from monopolistic control.
units.literal: Salt and iron should all return to the people.

units.zh: 去奴婢，除專殺之威。
units.en: He also called for reducing coercive private domination.
units.literal: Remove slave categories and eliminate power of arbitrary killing.

units.zh: 薄賦斂，省繇役，以寬民力。
units.en: Tax and labor burdens should be reduced to restore social stamina.
units.literal: Lighten taxes and levies, reduce corvée, to relax people's strength.

units.zh: 然後可善治也。」
units.en: Only under those conditions could stable good government emerge."
units.literal: Only then can governance be good."

units.zh: 戊戌，以新除冠軍將軍張沖為郢州刺史，守五兵尚書陸慧曉為南兖州刺史。
units.en: Day wuxu: Zhang Chong, newly made champion general, took Ying; Lu Huixiao, acting minister of the five arms, took South Yan.
units.literal: Day wuxu: the newly appointed Champion General Zhang Chong was made Inspector of Yingzhou; Acting Minister of the Five Arms Lu Huixiao was made Inspector of South Yanzhou.

units.zh: 太祖入奉大統，上及議者皆疑不敢下，曇首與到彥之、從兄華固勸，上猶未許。
units.en: The prince went in to accept the great succession. The emperor and his advisers were all afraid and hesitated to step down. Tanshou, Dao Yanzhi, and his cousin Hua pressed him hard, but the emperor still would not agree.
units.literal: The Taizu entered to receive the great succession. The Emperor and all who deliberated were doubtful and dared not descend. Tanshou with Dao Yanzhi and his cousin Hua firmly urged him, but the Emperor still did not assent.

units.zh: 遷司徒刑獄參軍事，入爲尚書殿中郎，轉司徒竟陵王記室參軍，以父憂去職。
units.en: He rose to prison staff in the criminal office, then palace attendant in the secretariat, then recorder to the Prince of Jingling, and left for his father's mourning.
units.literal: Promoted to Criminal Office Prison staff officer, entered as Attendant of the Palace Department in the Masters of Writing, then transferred to Staff Officer and Recorder to the Prince of Jingling of the Secretariat, left office for father's mourning.

units.zh: 始高祖與昉遇竟陵王西邸，從容謂昉曰：「我登三府，當以卿爲記室。」
units.en: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's western residence, he said lightly, "When I reach the three offices, you shall be my recorder."
units.literal: When Gaozu first met Fang at the Prince of Jingling's Western Residence, he said with ease: "When I rise to the three offices, I shall make you my recorder."

units.zh: 賾與河南元善、河東柳䛒、太原王劭、吳興姚察、琅琊諸葛潁、信都劉焯、河間劉炫相善，每因休假，清談竟日。
units.en: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.
units.literal: Ze was on good terms with Yuan Shan of Henan, Liu Bi of Hedong, Wang Shao of Taiyuan, Yao Cha of Wuxing, Zhuge Ying of Langya, Liu Zhuo of Xindu, and Liu Xuan of Hejian; on holidays they would converse in pure talk all day.
